clue.text: Better, a civic role

parts.note: to cap something is to better or outdo it
civic means relating to a city, read here as the city itself

explanation.surface: Someone praises a public civic post as an improvement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like an adjective but is the verb CAP, as in capping someone's story.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in an official capacity means acting in a particular role or position, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Communist leader inspired by rhetoric, as Trotsky

indicators.note: inspired by means breathed in by, so the name sits within the following words

explanation.surface: A Communist leader is inspired by Trotsky's rhetoric.
explanation.definitionFit: Fidel Castro led Communist Cuba for decades, an example of a Communist leader.

clue.text: Silver perhaps ending in skip, furious

indicators.note: ending in means the last letter of the word skip

parts.note: irate means furious

explanation.surface: Someone named Silver gets furious and skips off.
explanation.walkthrough: Long John Silver is the pirate in Treasure Island; 'perhaps' marks him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Long John Silver of Treasure Island is the classic fictional buccaneer, an example of the type.

clue.text: Revolutionary film showing drug-dealer

parts.note: Che Guevara was the Argentine-born revolutionary
a film is a thin layer or haze, as is a mist

explanation.surface: A revolutionary film depicts a drug-dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' suggests a movie, but it is a haze. 'drug-dealer' sounds criminal but is legitimate.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharmacist legitimately sells medicines, so the shop's trade is literally dealing in drugs.

clue.text: Rwanda confused with teeny part of northern England

indicators.note: confused means the letters of the two words are jumbled together

explanation.surface: Someone mixes up Rwanda with a tiny corner of northern England.
explanation.walkthrough: TYNE AND WEAR is a metropolitan county around Newcastle and Sunderland in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: This county surrounding Newcastle lies in the north-east, a region of northern England.

clue.text: A wave on top

parts.note: a swell is a long rolling wave at sea

explanation.surface: A surfer's request: a wave on top of the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean in addition, additionally, as an extra besides.

clue.text: Fight and fight for bird

parts.note: to spar is to box or fight
a row is a quarrel or fight

explanation.surface: Two birds fight and fight over something.
explanation.definitionFit: A sparrow is a small brown songbird, an example of a bird.

clue.text: One into old maps makes things clear

parts.note: ex means former or old

indicators.note: into means the numeral goes inside the following words

parts.note: plans are maps or diagrams
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: One person studies old maps and clarifies matters.
explanation.definitionFit: To explain is to make something clear and understandable, so the verb and phrase match.

clue.text: Continent with mountains primarily toured by girl

indicators.note: toured by means the girl goes all around the pieces

parts.note: lass is a word for a girl
and means with or along with

indicators.note: primarily means only the first letter of the word mountains

explanation.surface: A girl tours a continent and its mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: A continent is a large continuous expanse of land, so this is a near synonym.

clue.text: Policeman enters a complex carrying gun, initially

indicators.note: carrying means the jumbled letters hold the next piece inside them
complex means intricately tangled, so the letters of the two words are mixed up
initially means only the opening letter of the word gun is used

explanation.surface: An officer walks into a building complex armed with a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' looks like a noun for a building but scrambles ENTERS A into SEREANT; 'carrying' puts G inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sergeant is a rank of police officer, so this is an example of a policeman.

clue.text: A politician in office, wet

indicators.note: in means the first pieces are placed inside the room

parts.note: a den is a small private room or study used as an office
MP stands for Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A soggy politician sits in an office, perhaps a feeble 'wet' Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wet' reads as an insult for a weak politician, but it is the verb defining the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To dampen something is to make it slightly moist, so it is a synonym for the verb wet.

clue.text: Bit of a looker quaffing second wine

indicators.note: quaffing means drinking, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: a looker is an eye, and the retina is part of it

explanation.surface: An attractive person is drinking a second glass of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looker' suggests an attractive person; here it is literally an eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin, an example of the category.

clue.text: Structure that may pop in solid weapon

indicators.note: in means the popping structure is placed inside the word for solid

parts.note: firm means solid or hard
ears are structures that pop with changes in pressure

explanation.surface: Something that pops sits inside a solid weapon, like a cartridge in a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A firearm is a gun, a kind of weapon that fires bullets.

clue.text: Lively — as soy sauce?

definitions.meaning: energetic, bubbly and full of energy
soy sauce is made from soya beans, so it literally contains a lot of them

explanation.surface: Is lively soy sauce the right comparison?
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means energetic and exuberant, while soy sauce is literally brewed from beans.

clue.text: Game attempts to give flirty signal when squiffy?

parts.note: squiffy and tiddly are both British slang for slightly drunk
a wink is a flirty signal with one eye, and winks are attempts at giving it

explanation.surface: Someone tipsy tries winking flirtatiously at another person.
explanation.walkthrough: TIDDLY is British slang for tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiddlywinks is a parlour game of flicking small discs into a cup.

clue.text: Trustworthy hand

definitions.meaning: in poker, five cards in sequence

explanation.surface: A dependable hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight means honest, and in poker it is a hand of five consecutive cards.

clue.text: Drinking last of vermouth, I bemoan lamentable free spirit

indicators.note: drinking means the reworked letters take in the next piece
lamentable means wretched or poor, so the letters are reworked
last of means only the final letter of the word vermouth

explanation.surface: Someone drinking vermouth bemoans their sad state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lamentable' turns I BEMOAN into BOEMIAN, and 'Drinking' takes H inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bohemian lives an unconventional artistic life, a free spirit by nature.

clue.text: Difficult book about foreign money

indicators.note: about means the book surrounds the money

parts.note: a tome is a large book
roubles are the currency of Russia

explanation.surface: A hard book about foreign currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'on the subject of', but it means going around.
explanation.definitionFit: Something troublesome causes difficulty, so it is a synonym for difficult.

clue.text: Million-dollar contract? I'm not impressed!

definitions.meaning: a sarcastic retort meaning so what

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off news of a million-dollar contract.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a large business agreement and, ironically, a dismissive so what.

clue.text: Sporting call angered drunk

indicators.note: drunk means the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: An angry drunk shouts at a sports match.
explanation.definitionFit: A fencer calls this to warn an opponent to take guard before a bout.

clue.text: Needing lots of determination at first to turn over, old generator

indicators.note: to turn over means the pieces before it are read backwards

parts.note: lots means many

indicators.note: at first means the opening letter of the word determination

explanation.surface: A determined effort is needed to crank an old generator into life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn over' reverses MANY + D into DYNAM; O follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo is an electrical generator producing direct current.

clue.text: Rotten count was commanding

parts.note: to add is to count up
led means was in command

explanation.surface: A rotten aristocrat, a count, was in command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'count' looks like a nobleman, but it is the verb to sum up.
explanation.definitionFit: An addled egg has gone bad, so addled means rotten.

clue.text: Nemesis, England invading state

indicators.note: invading means the abbreviation goes inside the verb for state

parts.note: to aver is to state or assert

explanation.surface: England's forces invade another state, which becomes their nemesis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks like a country, but it is the verb meaning to declare.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis was the Greek goddess of retribution, so a nemesis is one who takes vengeance.

clue.text: Bewildered, guy struggling to keep tail of snake in the sack

indicators.note: in means all the rest goes inside the word for sack

parts.note: the sack is slang for bed

indicators.note: to keep means the jumbled letters hold another piece
struggling suggests the letters writhe into a new order
tail of means the final letter of the word snake

explanation.surface: A man wrestles a snake in bed and is left bewildered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the sack' is slang for bed. 'struggling' makes UGY, 'to keep' wraps it round the snake's tail, and 'in' sends the lot into the sack.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with eyes bulging in astonishment looks bewildered, a figurative synonym.

clue.text: Country that's worth more than a pound?

definitions.meaning: the old British gold coin was worth 21 shillings, a shilling more than a pound

explanation.surface: Which nation's value exceeds a pound sterling?
explanation.walkthrough: The old British guinea coin was worth one pound and one shilling.
explanation.definitionFit: Guinea names both an African republic and a former British coin worth twenty-one shillings.

clue.text: 'Cats' problem, musical delivery?

parts.note: Hair is a 1960s rock musical
in cricket a ball is a single delivery from the bowler

explanation.surface: Trouble with a production of the musical Cats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cats' looks like the musical, but it is real cats; the musical is HAIR. In cricket a delivery is a BALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Cats groom themselves and cough up wads of swallowed fur, a familiar feline problem.

clue.text: Trap finally caught fish

indicators.note: finally means only the last letter of the word caught

parts.note: to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: A trap finally caught a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To tangle someone is to ensnare or entrap them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: A drug that builds muscle for heavenly body

parts.note: anabolic steroids are drugs used to build muscle

explanation.surface: A bodybuilder's drug produces a heavenly body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heavenly body' suggests a sculpted physique, but it is an object in space.
explanation.definitionFit: An asteroid is a small rocky body orbiting the sun, an example of a celestial object.
